## Learning goals

You will read a difference in means as an effect of assignment. The file is the social-pressure turnout experiment in QSS 2.4 (Gerber, Green, and Larimer). Households were randomly assigned to a mailing. `messages` is the mailing. `primary2006` is 1 if someone in the household voted in the 2006 primary. The comparison below is the Neighbors mailing against Control.

## 1. Setup

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
social <- read_csv("data/social.csv")
social %>%
  filter(messages %in% c("Control", "Neighbors")) %>%
  group_by(messages) %>%
  summarise(turnout = mean(primary2006), n = n(), .groups = "drop")
```

Control turnout is about 29.7 percent. The Neighbors mailing is about 37.8 percent. The difference is about 8.1 percentage points.

What was randomized is the mailing, not the vote. Under random assignment, that difference estimates the average effect of being assigned the Neighbors mailing in this experiment. It does not, by itself, say that the same mailing would do the same thing in another election, or which feeling inside the household produced the vote.
